title: Continuous Wearage
description: User continuously wears the device, providing constant access to sensor data.
assumptions: User is aware of the device and its purpose.

title: Continuous Data Collection
description: Device continuously captures and transmits sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS, timestamps) to the external entity.
assumptions: Device functionality is assumed to be reliable and uninterrupted.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Device (P1) transfers personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps) to the Companion Mobile App (P2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the device is transferring personal data to a known third party (the app).

title: Data Disclosure
description: Companion Mobile App (P2) receives and processes personal data from the Device (P1). This involves the transfer of personal data from a known third party (the device) to the app, which is a data disclosure.

title: Unawareness as a user sharing personal data
description: The user (ExternalEntity EE1) does not need to be the data subject for the data to be processed. The user is merely a conduit for the data to be entered into the Companion Mobile App (Process P2).
assumptions: The user is not the data subject.

title: Unawareness as a process sharing personal data
description: The Companion Mobile App (Process P2) does not need to be the data subject for the data to be processed. The app is merely a conduit for the data to be entered by the user.
assumptions: The app is not the data subject.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the app transfers personal health data to a third-party data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Log Store (DS1) receives and stores health logs from the Companion Mobile App (P2). This represents a data disclosure where the store is the recipient of personal health data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the app transfers personal data (location traces) to a third-party data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Location History Store (DS2) receives data from the Companion Mobile App (P2). This is a data disclosure as the store receives personal data from a third-party process.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Health Log Store (DS1) transfers personal health data (calories, weight, exercise logs) to the Health Analytics Service (P3) for processing. This constitutes a data disclosure as the store is transferring data to a third party (the analytics service) for health-condition analysis.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and designed for the analytics service to process the logs.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Health Analytics Service (P3) receives and processes personal health data from the Health Log Store (DS1). This involves the transfer of personal data from the store to the service, which is a data disclosure.
assumptions: The service is processing the logs as intended.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) queries the Location History Store (DS2) to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This interaction involves the transfer of personal location data from the data store to the analytics process, which may constitute a data disclosure if the data is considered personal and the transfer is not strictly necessary for the analytics function.
assumptions: The data being transferred is personal location history.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the data is strictly personal or if the transfer is considered a 'necessary' disclosure under the minimality principle.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) queries the Location History Store (DS2). The threat is located at the originator (P3) because the process itself initiates the data flow to the data store, which is a data disclosure event.
assumptions: The process is designed to access location data for analytics purposes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the process is considered a 'known third party' or if the data is strictly required for the analytics function.

title: Profiling a group of individuals
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) processes health-condition risk indicators and trend flags, which are personal data related to specific individuals. By aggregating these indicators, the service infers insights about a larger group of individuals (e.g., identifying a cohort with similar risk profiles). This constitutes a Linking threat where data of a single individual leads to insights about a larger group through known relations of group membership or similarity.
assumptions: The health indicators are personal data and the aggregation logic relies on group membership or similarity relations.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) receives health-condition risk indicators and trend flags from the Health Analytics Service (P3). This represents a Data Disclosure threat where personal health data is transmitted from a process to an external entity (the app) without appropriate safeguards, potentially leading to the exposure of sensitive health information.
assumptions: The data transmitted to the app is considered personal health data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The companion mobile app (Process P2) is transmitting user data (e.g., inferred condition indicators, eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to an external entity (User/EE1). This constitutes a data disclosure threat where sensitive health information is being shared outside the controlled system boundary.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The external entity (User/EE1) is receiving and processing data from the process (P2). This represents a data disclosure threat where the external user is accessing and potentially sharing sensitive health-related data.

title: Data Disclosure to Cloud Hosting Provider
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) transfers analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset to the Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data to a third party.

title: Data Disclosure from Cloud Hosting Provider
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2) is receiving and storing the Health Analytics Service's data, which may constitute a data disclosure if the provider is considered a third party outside the system boundary.
